rounds.response: 169.254.x.x means your PC failed to get a DHCP lease from the router (APIPA). First try forget + reconnect the Wi‑Fi network (Settings → Network & Internet → Wi‑Fi → Manage known networks → Forget), and turn off “Random hardware addresses” for that SSID. Then open an admin Command Prompt and run: ipconfig /release && ipconfig /renew && sc query Dhcp (verify the DHCP Client service is RUNNING in Services.msc); if /renew still returns 169.254, temporarily assign a static IP on the router subnet (example if your router is 192.168.1.1): netsh interface ip set address name="Wi‑Fi" static 192.168.1.50 255.255.255.0 192.168.1.1 && netsh interface ip set dns name="Wi‑Fi" static 8.8.8.8 then ping 192.168.1.1. If a static IP still can’t reach the gateway, reinstall the Wi‑Fi driver (Device Manager → Network adapters → uninstall device → reboot) and disable the adapter’s power‑saving option (Properties → Power Management → uncheck), and if possible try Ethernet or reboot the router and check its DHCP client list/blacklist; paste the outputs of ipconfig /all and the ping results if you want me to analyze them.
